llmAnalysis.summary: Well-hardened bar widget that wraps bundled helpers (mx-ctl/mx-buttons → solaar) with strict caps, plain-text sanitization and safe bash positional parameters. No unauthenticated IPC or injection surface; only intentional local code execution is the user-typed Custom button command which is explicitly user-authorized.
llmAnalysis.whatItDoes: Bar widget and panel for a Bluetooth-paired Logitech MX Master 3S. Shows connection/battery/host and lets the user tune DPI, SmartShift threshold, scroll ratchet/invert/hi-res and reassign thumb/gesture buttons. All writes go to the mouse's onboard memory via Solaar, so they persist across reboots and travel with the mouse to its other paired hosts.
llmAnalysis.sequenceDiagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Panel as Panel.qml
    participant Ctl as mx-ctl (bash)
    participant Btn as mx-buttons (python)
    participant Solaar
    participant Mouse as MX Master 3S
    User->>Panel: open panel / toggle / drag slider
    Panel->>Ctl: Process bash -c 'MX_DEVICE="$1" "$0" status [--battery]' ctl deviceName
    Ctl->>Solaar: solaar config/show DEVICE
    Solaar->>Mouse: HID++ query
    Mouse-->>Solaar: settings + battery
    Solaar-->>Ctl: text output
    Ctl-->>Panel: key=value lines (capped, parseStatus)
    Panel-->>User: render battery/DPI/hosts (Model.plain/snapDpi)
    User->>Panel: set DPI / toggle / change-host
    Panel->>Ctl: Process bash -c 'MX_DEVICE="$1" "$0" set "$2" "$3"' ctl deviceName key value
    Ctl->>Solaar: solaar config DEVICE key value
    Solaar->>Mouse: write onboard memory
    User->>Panel: set button action (incl. Custom command)
    Panel->>Btn: Process bash -c 'MX_DEVICE="$1" "$0" set ...' buttonsCtl deviceName name action command
    Btn->>Solaar: solaar config divert-keys/reprogrammable-keys + regenerate ~/.config/solaar/rules.yaml (yaml_str escaped)
    Btn->>Solaar: restart daemon (SIGTERM + Popen hide)
    Note over Btn,Solaar: Later button press → Solaar Execute: [bash,-c, command]

findings.reasoning: Registers bar-widget IPC name for Omarchy shell routing; no custom message handler or payload parsing is defined in Panel.qml (no onIpc/message handler), so static flag's assumed conditional validation does not apply – exposure is inherent to framework and benign here.

Not just a path resolve – Qt.resolvedUrl("mx-ctl") (and line 88 "mx-buttons") locates bundled executables later run via Process command with safe bash -c 'MX_DEVICE="$1" "$0" ...' positional-arg pattern; args (deviceName, keys, snapped DPI) are quoted as "$1"/"$2"/"$3" and capped via Model.capInput/plain, so no shell injection despite being an exec sink.
findings.relatedCode: readonly property string ctl: String(Qt.resolvedUrl("mx-ctl")).replace("file://", "") // used as statusProc.command = ["bash","-c","MX_DEVICE=\"$1\" \"$0\" status --battery", root.ctl, root.deviceName] and writeProc/buttonSetProc/buttonsProc similarly with root.buttonsCtl
findings.executableContext: mx-ctl is bundled bash wrapper around `solaar config/show` that reads/writes MX Master settings (dpi, smart-shift, scroll modes, change-host) to the mouse's onboard memory and queries battery; mx-buttons is bundled Python helper that maps actions.json (gestures/remap/command/custom) to solaar divert-keys/reprogrammable-keys and rebuilds ~/.config/solaar/rules.yaml with yaml_str-escaped Execute:[bash,-c, command] rules – Custom kind intentionally runs user-typed shell command on button press (user-authorized local exec, truncated to 2048 chars)
